topics.inclusion_rule: Studies that train a decoder of speech acoustics (or speech units) from a non-acoustic signal using target speech that the user did not produce: text-to-speech output, a reference speaker's recording, or a voice-converted or pre-injury voice, because the user cannot produce intelligible audio. Boundary: exclude targets recorded from the same user during the same or a paired vocalized trial (paired audio, DTW target transfer); exclude text-only targets; count versions of one study once.
topics.metric: listener or ASR WER of synthesized speech

topics.inclusion_rule: Speech synthesis from a non-acoustic signal (EMG, ultrasound, articulography, video, neural) whose training adds a phoneme, phone-state, CTC or text classification loss on a shared encoder that is discarded or used only as guidance at synthesis time. Boundary: recognition-only models, cascaded recognize-then-TTS systems, and regression-only auxiliary targets are excluded; versions counted once.

Surface-EMG speech synthesis or voicing studies (EMG to audible speech), classified by the intermediate target the EMG model predicts before the waveform: spectral acoustic features (mel, MFCC, vocoder parameters), self-supervised speech units, articulatory features (EMA-type trajectories), or text/phonemes. Boundary: EMG recognition to text only, EMG as an auxiliary channel to audio, non-speech EMG and reviews are excluded when read; a study can use several targets; versions count once.

Surface-EMG decoders whose output is scored with WER or CER (recognition, or ASR on synthesized speech); the design compared is whether the headline error is measured on sentences absent from all training data (sentence-disjoint, open vocabulary) or on repeats of training sentences (closed set). Boundary: a paper is counted under each protocol its text names; reviews count as pattern matches only; versions of one study count once.
